model.title: Prediction Accuracy
model.subtitle: How good is the AI model, checked against real held-out test data.
model.aiModelExplainBody: AgriRoute AI uses a model called XGBoost, trained to guess how likely a crop is to spoil, based on the crop type, the temperature, and how many days since harvest.
model.featureImportanceNote: How much each factor actually drives the AI model's guess, from the trained model itself.
model.classificationExplain: The AI gives a 0-100 risk score, not just "spoiled" or "not spoiled". These numbers are worked out by treating a score of {{threshold}} or more as "spoiled", using the model's real answers on test data it hadn't seen before.
model.confusionMatrixNote: What the AI guessed vs. what actually happened, on test data.
model.notAvailable: Not available yet — retrain the model to see this.
model.representativeBatchesNote: Real batches with a farmer-recorded actual sale, compared against what the model predicted at that time. Not a synthetic demonstration.
model.representativeBatchesEmpty: No batches with a recorded actual sale yet. This table populates as farmers record real outcomes.

data.title: Where This Information Comes From
data.subtitle: What's real, what's a good estimate, and what's sample data — nothing here is hidden.
data.networkSubtitle: Every market and cold storage we know about, not tied to one crop check.
data.hackathonNote: This is a hackathon-stage project. Real historical spoilage outcomes from real farmer pilots and live per-facility storage occupancy are still future roadmap items — not implemented here, and never shown as if they were.
data.relatedSystemsTitle: How This Differs From Existing Systems
data.relatedSystemsSubtitle: Named for comparison, not to claim this is the only tool in this space.
data.relatedEnam: Government e-market platform digitizing 1,000+ mandis for price discovery and trading; doesn't predict spoilage risk or recommend where to route a specific batch.
data.relatedNinjacart: Supply-chain logistics connecting farmers directly to retailers/businesses; focused on fulfillment and traceability, not a per-batch spoilage-risk model.
data.relatedDehaat: End-to-end farmer platform (inputs, advisory, credit, market linkage); market linkage is general, not driven by a trained spoilage-risk model comparing specific destinations.
data.relatedAgribazaar: Farmer-buyer marketplace that reduces time-to-sale by cutting out middlemen; doesn't rank destinations by predicted spoilage-adjusted realised value.
data.relatedDifferentiation: This project's specific contribution is the integration: a trained spoilage-risk model feeding directly into a per-destination economic ranking (expected realised value = revenue − transport − storage − predicted spoilage loss), validated against nearest-market/highest-price/price-minus-distance baselines on the Prediction Accuracy page. It is not claimed to be the only tool addressing post-harvest loss in India.
